page: Microsoft Azure D8ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory allocation stands at 32.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support features AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though it lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Local storage includes a bundled 322 GB SSD alongside support for Azure Premium Storage.

Benchmark results show balanced computational capabilities with notable single-core strength. The instance achieves a top-quartile stress-ng single-core score of 2,701.98, while multi-core stress-ng records 10,797.67 in the mid-range tier. Geekbench 6 metrics reflect solid general compute with 1,494.0 in single-core and 5,866.0 in multi-core execution. Memory subsystems demonstrate high throughput for cached 16 KB read blocks at 514.81 GB/sec, though uncached 256 MB block operations place in the lower quartile with 39.11 GB/sec read and 22.63 GB/sec write bandwidths.

In operational benchmark profiles, the instance delivered 8.16 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, 9.82 GB/sec static web serving throughput, and a PassMark database operations metric of 3,558.43. Small-model language inference reaches 566.65 prompt tokens per second and 221.85 generation tokens per second. Given its balanced resource footprint and integrated local SSD scratch space, the D8ads_v5 offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for relational databases, enterprise web servers, continuous integration build nodes, and general backend application environments.
description: Microsoft Azure D8ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory allocation. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at 3.525 GHz across 4 physical cores with multithreading, it includes 32 MB of L3 cache alongside a bundled 322 GB local SSD. Compute performance is highlighted by strong single-core execution in stress-ng benchmarks (2,701.98), paired with balanced overall multi-core throughput in Geekbench and PassMark suites. While uncached large-block memory bandwidth exhibits moderate constraints, the instance delivers steady throughput for transactional and I/O workloads, clocking 8.16 million Redis SET operations per second and 9.82 GB/sec in static web serving. The instance lacks dedicated GPU accelerators, making it suitable for web applications, relational databases, caching tiers, and software build pipelines requiring fast temporary local storage.
